raw_case_text: The patient is a 37-year-old Chinese male. In April 2014, he was diagnosed with brucellosis due to fever and fatigue, and his symptoms disappeared after anti-brucellosis medications for three months. In October 2014, the patient developed left hip pain, worsened by weight-bearing, and was admitted to the orthopedics department of our hospital in December 2014 due to the deterioration of symptoms. He is a sheep herdsman without any history of trauma, alcoholism, or hormone use. Physical examination revealed that the active and passive motion of the left hip was somewhat restricted due to pain. X-ray demonstrated that the left femoral head exhibited a strip-like low-density area but no evidence of stenosis (Figure 1A and B). CT scan revealed cavity necrosis in the left femoral head (Figure 1C). MRI revealed necrosis of the left femoral head, and effusion in the left joint cavity (Figure 1D and E). Blood test showed WBC 6.85 x 109/L with neutrophils accounted for 61.8%, CRP 3.5 mg/L, ESR 2.00 mm/h. SAT was positive at a titer of 1:320, and all tests for tuberculosis and rheumatoid arthritis were negative. Having been diagnosed with brucellar hip arthritis complicated by osteonecrosis of the left femoral head, the patient underwent puncture and irrigation of the left hip joint and core decompression and bone grafting. B. melitensis was detected in hip joint effusion and osteonecrosis of femoral head by real-time PCR. HE staining of a core biopsy of the left femoral head revealed amorphous necrotic material (Figure 2A); Giemsa staining can demonstrate scattered positive Brucella (Figure 2B). Triple anti-infective therapy was administered after the operation: rifampicin (0.6g po qd; Guangdong Hengjian Pharmaceuticals), doxycycline (0.1g po bid; Jiangsu Lianhuan Pharmaceuticals), and levofloxacin (0.2g ivgtt bid; Yangtze River Pharmaceuticals). Upon discharge from the hospital two weeks after the operation, his left hip pain was substantially relieved, and the antibiotic regimen was adjusted to rifampicin (0.6g po qd; Guangdong Hengjian Pharmaceuticals) and doxycycline (0.1g po bid; Jiangsu Lianhuan Pharmaceuticals) for six months. In follow-up, the symptoms of left hip pain and movement limitation disappeared almost half a year later, and there was no obvious abnormality in the blood test or hip X-ray (Figure 1F). In the telephone follow-up in April 2022, the patient's recovery proceeded well.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old Chinese male sheep herdsman with a history of brucellosis 8 months earlier presented in December 2014 with a 2-month history of progressive weight-bearing left hip pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 37-year-old male sheep herdsman who had been treated for febrile brucellosis for 3 months in April 2014 developed progressive left hip pain aggravated by weight-bearing in October 2014, leading to orthopedic admission in December 2014.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic brucellosis diagnosed in April 2014 and treated for 3 months; occupational exposure as a sheep herdsman. Denied trauma, alcoholism, or corticosteroid use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive weight-bearing left hip pain and restricted hip mobility; negative for recurrent fever.

objective.physical_examination: Painful restriction of both active and passive range of motion of the left hip joint.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 6.85 x 10^9/L (61.8% neutrophils), CRP 3.5 mg/L, ESR 2.00 mm/h; negative tests for tuberculosis and rheumatoid arthritis. Left hip X-ray showed a strip-like radiolucent/low-density area in the left femoral head without joint space narrowing.
objective.advanced_workup: Left hip CT demonstrated cavitary osteonecrosis of the left femoral head; left hip MRI confirmed avascular necrosis of the left femoral head with a left hip joint effusion. Histopathology (H&E) of the left femoral head core biopsy showed amorphous necrotic bone, Giemsa staining demonstrated scattered intracellular Brucella organisms, and real-time PCR of both the hip joint effusion and necrotic femoral head core tissue identified Brucella melitensis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Positive serum agglutination test (SAT titer 1:320), Giemsa staining, and real-time PCR of the left hip joint aspirate and femoral head core biopsy identifying Brucella melitensis confirmed brucellar left hip arthritis complicated by osteonecrosis of the left femoral head. Treated with left hip joint puncture and irrigation, femoral head core decompression and bone grafting, and 2 weeks of inpatient triple therapy with oral rifampicin (0.6 g QD), oral doxycycline (0.1 g BID), and IV levofloxacin (0.2 g BID), followed by 6 months of outpatient oral rifampicin and doxycycline. Left hip pain and motion restriction resolved completely by 6 months, with sustained recovery at April 2022 follow-up.
